sections.title: In brief
sections.text: A parametric grammar reconstructs main features of Palladio’s villa ground plans. The worked Villa Malcontenta example makes an architectural style explicit as a generative process.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: Can a style description both explain existing plans and provide rules for producing further plans with related structure?

sections.title: Main idea or claim
sections.text: A generative account should support description, recognition and synthesis. The proposed grammar is a partial definition of Palladian style based on plans in the Quattro Libri.

sections.title: How the work approaches it
sections.text: Eight stages define a grid, exterior walls, rooms, wall realignment, entrances, exterior ornamentation, windows/doors and termination. Labels and parameter constraints preserve relationships such as bilateral symmetry.

sections.title: Evidence and examples
sections.text: Rules are motivated by Palladio’s stated prescriptions and published plan examples. A full illustrated derivation produces Malcontenta’s plan; the discussion sketches extension to biaxial villas.

sections.title: What comes out of it
sections.text: The case demonstrates how a finite rule repertoire can explain an existing plan and define a larger design language. It shows a constructive model of style rather than only a visual resemblance classification.

sections.title: Limits to keep in mind
sections.text: Facades and a complete proportional system are outside scope. The precise parameterization is not supplied. The authors acknowledge corpus choices, drawing inconsistencies and judgments about minor variations; this is not evidence of Palladio’s actual mental design sequence.

sections.title: What to take from it
sections.text: Read the rules alongside the source plans. Separate what the grammar reproduces, what it deliberately simplifies, and which new plans it allows beyond the historical corpus.
